selection_rule: Frozen before the closed diagnostic: for each of the three contexts the production generator is the one with minimum mean SWD on the 35-beer validation split. The test split is never used to select a generator, and the closed diagnostic was not allowed to re-select.
interpretation: The reversal is a resolution effect, not a contradiction. CVAE is closer only where a style has one or two independent test beers (13/13 and 12/12 pairs); its advantage shrinks monotonically as the test set grows (-0.242, -0.168, -0.081, -0.011) and it wins only 4/6 at n_test>=5. The gap correlates with n_test at r=0.703. CVAE is simultaneously the most degenerate generator: diversity 0.420 versus 0.897 for the shipped independent Copula, and nearest-train RMS 0.681 versus 1.114, i.e. it sits close to a small-sample empirical distribution, which is exactly what makes a Wasserstein distance look small when the empirical side has almost no resolution. Model choice therefore follows the frozen validation rule and is defended on diversity/floor-matching, not on the conditional SWD column; quoting the closed table alone would reverse a decision that was made before it existed.
what_would_overturn_this: If CVAE kept its SWD advantage on styles with >=5 independent test beers, the frozen selection would be wrong. It does not: at n_test>=5 the gap is -0.011 and Copula wins 2 of 6. Only 6 such pairs exist, so this is a direction, not a decisive test.
